question: Should OpenClaw add a plugin-visible skill install/update completion observer now, and what redacted payload plus observer-failure semantics should it expose?
rationale: Automation can prove the missing lifecycle surface, but choosing what install metadata plugins may see and whether observer failures can affect an already-written install is a security and product boundary decision.

options.title: Add minimal observer
options.body: Add a non-blocking completion hook with redacted source, provenance, target, outcome, and timestamp metadata plus documented fail-open logging semantics.

options.title: Declare pre-install sufficient
options.body: Treat `security.installPolicy` and `before_install` as the complete install security answer, then narrow or close the audit-observer part separately.

options.title: Defer to ClawHub trust design
options.body: Hold the observer until maintainers define a broader ClawHub trust/provenance API that can supply the same audit events.

recommendation.title: Add minimal observer
recommendation.body: Add a non-blocking completion hook with redacted source, provenance, target, outcome, and timestamp metadata plus documented fail-open logging semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses ClawHub skill install behavior and the existing install-security gate path, both tied to steipete in recent history.
